_note: Canonical object-lifetime roles, as DATA. The reader emits alloc/dealloc lifecycle events (the typestate skeleton the matcher walks for double-free / use-after-free / leak) from THIS file -- so teaching it a new kernel allocator or free is an edit here, never a code change in the engine. Roles are memory-lifecycle facts, not taint sink/source roles, which is why they live in their own detection-layer catalog rather than the models/ sink tree.
_derivation_note: Sized allocators are NOT re-listed here: any sink in models/<lang> whose kind is in `alloc_kinds` (e.g. kmalloc, kzalloc, kcalloc -- all `alloc-size`) is already an allocation, and those models stay the single source of truth for it. The `alloc` lists below add only the size-LESS allocators (strdup-family: they return an owned pointer but carry no explicit size argument, so they never appear in the sized-sink catalog).
_realloc_note: `realloc`-family calls are BOTH: they free the block their first argument names (it may be relocated) AND return a fresh allocation. They keep their `alloc-size` sink identity in the models/ catalog (their size argument is still a spatial sink), and the `realloc` list below adds the lifetime fact the catalog cannot carry -- that the old generation is (may-be) freed. An interior pointer or alias captured before the realloc and not rebased to the returned pointer dangles: a use-after-free the reader emits from this datum with no bug-specific engine logic. First argument = the reallocated pointer.
_aggregate_copy_note: Aggregate-copy roles identify calls whose size/form proves a whole object is copied. The reader expands these calls into field-wise alias facts; ordinary byte-buffer copies remain spatial operations only.
